name: TOLEDO INNOVATION CENTER LANDLORD LLC
entity_filed: Not the grant payee. Toledo Innovation Center Landlord LLC filed nothing and is not a debtor. The entities that filed are the operating partner and its parent: Bitwise Industries, Inc. (EIN 47-1635652) and BW Industries Inc. (EIN 84-2292459), together with BWRD, LLC, Alpha Works Technologies, LLC and Bruce's Bagels, Beverages, and Bites, LLC. All five filed Chapter 7 liquidation, not Chapter 11, on 2023-06-28. JobsOhio's own project record names the counterparty as 'Bitwise, Inc. (BW Industries Inc.)', which is debtor 23-10844.
court: United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware
docket: 23-10845-TMH (Bitwise Industries, Inc.); 23-10844-TMH (BW Industries Inc.); 23-10846 through 23-10848 for the three affiliates. Related: SEC v. Soberal and Olguin, E.D. Cal., RECAP gov.uscourts.caed.437121.
ohio_outcome: The operating company closed its Toledo sites and 18 Ohio jobs were lost; the building the money paid for was finished and is open today. Bitwise's own WARN letter of 2023-06-14, signed by interim president Ollen Douglass, says Bitwise will terminate 625 employees nationally, that 18 of them are Ohio residents in Lucas County, and that the facilities being closed include '1300 Jefferson, Toledo, OH' and '413 Adams Street, Toledo, OH'. The letter gives the reason as 'unforeseeable business circumstances and other reasons', says the separations are permanent, and says there are no bumping rights and no bargaining representative. The 18 Ohio positions are named one by one and are a head-office set rather than a production floor: a senior vice president of city expansion, a vice president of Bitwise Toledo, a program manager, an account executive, a community catalyst, an events coordinator, an executive assistant, a financial analyst, a front desk receptionist, three janitorial staff, a senior software developer, a student support specialist, two tenant improvement staff, a lead generator and a security guard. Two weeks later the whole group filed Chapter 7. The building at 1300 Jefferson Avenue was completed anyway and opened in February 2025 as Innovation Post, with inaugural tenants and a ribbon cutting, and it was still filling space at the end of 2025. The 378 jobs JobsOhio's project record bought did not happen.
source: Ohio Department of Job and Family Services WARN notice 009-23-037, 'Bitwise Industries, Inc.', Toledo/Lucas, 18 affected, received 6/14/23 at 4:06pm, fetched and read in full at jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/pdf/Bitwise-Industries-Inc.pdf (2 pages). Chapter 7 voluntary petition, Official Form 201, Case 23-10845-TMH Doc 1, filed 06/28/23, 40 pages, read in full from the RECAP mirror at archive.org/download/gov.uscourts.deb.190196/gov.uscourts.deb.190196.1.0.pdf; the petition's own CM/ECF header stamp gives the case number and date, and box 3 gives EIN 47-1635652, the same FEIN Bitwise put on the Ohio WARN letter. Doc 3 and Doc 4 in the same case caption all five Chapter 7 debtors with their EINs. Doc 21, a notice of appearance filed 2023-07-11 by Kutak Rock LLP, appears for 'Toledo IC Investment Fund, LLC; PNC New Markets Investment Partners, LLC; PNC Community Partners, Inc.; PNC CDE 128, LLC; and SPE PNC Toledo Innovation Center Master Tenant LLC'. SEC v. Soberal complaint, 14 pages, read in full at archive.org/download/gov.uscourts.caed.437121/gov.uscourts.caed.437121.1.0.pdf. data/grants_raw.csv FY2023 row (TOLEDO INNOVATION CENTER LANDLORD LLC, EIN 87-1277852, 100 Madison Ave, Toledo, OH, $1,500,000). data/commitments_norm.csv 2022-Mar rows. Google News headlines used only for dates and outcomes: Toledo Blade, 'Port Authority finances $11M of Bitwise technology center', 2021-12-16; Toledo Blade, 'Bitwise Industries furloughs 900 employees nationally; Jefferson Center plans unclear', 2023-05-31; Toledo Blade, 'City of Toledo celebrates inaugural tenants for former Jefferson Center', 2025-02-20; City of Toledo, 'City, Community and Business Partners Celebrate Innovation Post Opening with Ribbon Cutting', 2025-02-20; Toledo Blade, 'Toledo's Innovation Post celebrates inaugural year with room to grow', 2025-12-31; PropertyShark listing headline, 'The Innovation Post - 1300 Jefferson Ave, Toledo, OH 43604', 2026-10-19.
notes: Four things have to be said plainly or this row is unfair to the people named on it. First, the grant payee did not fail and must not be written as though it did. Toledo Innovation Center Landlord LLC is a special-purpose property entity inside a New Markets Tax Credit structure, and the Chapter 7 file shows the rest of that structure: a PNC investment fund called Toledo IC Investment Fund LLC, a PNC community development entity, and a master tenant called SPE PNC Toledo Innovation Center Master Tenant LLC. Those parties appeared in Bitwise's bankruptcy as creditors and interested parties, which is exactly what a landlord side of a deal does when its tenant liquidates. Second, the money paid for a building, and the building worked. The $1,500,000 matches to the dollar the JobsOhio Revitalization Grant in JobsOhio's own March 2022 project record for 'Bitwise, Inc. (BW Industries Inc.)', Lucas County, Technology, 378 jobs created, $19,980,874 investment, alongside a separate $3,000,000 Revitalization Loan. A Revitalization Grant pays to bring a distressed building back, and the former Jefferson Center was brought back: it opened as Innovation Post in February 2025 and has tenants. The failure is the operator and the jobs, not the bricks. Third, 18 is not a mass layoff in Ohio and the post must not call it one. The mass layoff was national, 625 people across fourteen sites in seven states; Ohio's share was 18 head-office and support staff. The honest sentence is that the anchor tenant liquidated and the Toledo operation closed, costing 18 jobs against the 378 the project record promised. Fourth, do not imply the fraud touched JobsOhio's money. The SEC complaint against co-founders Jake Soberal and Irma Olguin, Jr. is about falsifying documents and misleading investors while raising about $70 million in 2022; it never mentions Ohio, Toledo or JobsOhio, and I read all 14 pages to check. The founders were later sentenced to prison. The gap I could not close: no property record confirms that Toledo Innovation Center Landlord LLC holds title to 1300 Jefferson Avenue. The link rests on the entity's name, on the PNC 'Toledo Innovation Center Master Tenant' entity sitting in Bitwise's Chapter 7, on the payee's Toledo address, on the $1,500,000 matching JobsOhio's Lucas County Revitalization Grant to Bitwise, and on the WARN letter naming 1300 Jefferson as a closed Bitwise facility. The Ohio Secretary of State business search was down for maintenance and the Internet Archive went offline mid-session, so I could not pull the filing or an archived deed. A reporter should pull the Lucas County deed for 1300 Jefferson Avenue before naming the landlord entity.
funded_site: The former Jefferson Center, 1300 Jefferson Avenue, Toledo, OH 43604 (Lucas County), redeveloped as the Toledo Innovation Center and now trading as Innovation Post. Inferred, not confirmed from a property record; see notes.
failed_site: Bitwise's Toledo operation at 1300 Jefferson Avenue and 413 Adams Street, Toledo (Lucas County), both named as closing in Bitwise's own WARN letter
recommend: Keep it, and make it the row about the operator rather than the landlord. It is the largest single payment in this batch at $1,500,000 and the clearest case of JobsOhio money going into a project whose partner liquidated in the same fiscal year it was drawn. Write it as: JobsOhio paid $1.5 million in its 2023 fiscal year toward a Toledo building whose tenant, Bitwise, filed for Chapter 7 liquidation on 28 June 2023, two weeks after telling the state it was cutting 18 Toledo jobs, and whose founders were later convicted of fraud; the building was finished and is open today, and the 378 jobs in JobsOhio's project record did not arrive. Do not label it a mass layoff. Before a reporter calls anyone, pull the Lucas County deed for 1300 Jefferson Avenue to confirm the payee entity is the owner.

name: TECHNICOTE INC
entity_filed: No insolvency filing. The employer is Technicote Inc., the grant payee itself, trading as Beontag after the Brazilian label manufacturer Beontag acquired it in September 2022. No bankruptcy petition was found and none is claimed in the notice. This is a permanent mass layoff at one plant, not a corporate insolvency.
ohio_outcome: A permanent mass layoff at the plant JobsOhio paid for, which stays open with fewer people. The notice, signed by Erin Bernhardt, Vice President of the Graphic and Label Materials Division, says the company 'will implement a mass layoff at the above-referenced facility' at 6206 Wolf Creek Pike, Trotwood, OH 45426, that 'the facility will remain open, with reduced operations', and that 'this layoff is expected to be permanent' with 'a limited number of employees' staying to support ongoing operations. Approximately 53 employees were affected from 2026-05-24. The job titles are production, not office: 12 Packers, 8 Slitter Operators, 8 Coater Operators, 4 Production Supervisors, 4 Quality and Lab Technicians, 3 Maintenance Technicians, 2 Material Handlers, 3 Shipping and Receiving, and single posts covering maintenance supervision and planning, environmental health and safety, adhesives coatings engineering, customer service, freight, IT, finance and janitorial. No bumping rights and no union. JobsOhio's own December 2023 project record for Technicote, Inc. is a Montgomery County Advanced Manufacturing project, 163 jobs created and 70 retained on a $58,900,000 investment with a $700,000 JobsOhio Economic Development Grant. The full $700,000 was drawn in two $350,000 payments, FY2024 and FY2025, and the cut came about ten months after the second one.
source: Ohio Department of Job and Family Services WARN notice, 'Technicote Inc dba Beontag', Trotwood/Montgomery, kind Layoff, 53 affected, received 3/25/2026 at 12:43pm, layoff date 5/24/2026, fetched and read in full at dam.assets.ohio.gov/image/upload/v1774539368/jfs.ohio.gov/warn/WARN%202026/TechnicoteIncdbaBeontag.pdf (2 pages, letter plus the full job-title schedule). data/grants_raw.csv FY2024 row (TECHNICOTE INC, EIN 34-1313085, 222 Mound Ave, Miamisburg, OH, $350,000) and FY2025 row (TECHNICOTE INC, EIN 34-1313085, 6206 Wolf Creek Pike, Trotwood, OH, $350,000). data/commitments_norm.csv 2023-Dec row. data/grant_conditions.csv FY2024 and FY2025 rows, both JobsOhio Economic Development Grant. Corroborating headlines, used for dates only: Dayton Business Journal, 'Beontag to lay off 53 employees at Trotwood facility less than 2 years after opening', 2026-03-30; WHIO TV, 'Trotwood manufacturer to lay off dozens of employees', 2026-03-30; Dayton Daily News, 'Trotwood company will lay off 53 workers', 2026-04-02; Dayton Business Journal, 'Brazilian manufacturer unveils $80 million facility in Trotwood, additional investments on the way', 2024-10-17; Labels & Labeling, 'Beontag acquires Technicote', 2022-09-07.
notes: This is the cleanest site match in the batch and needs no inference. The FY2025 Schedule I payment address, 6206 Wolf Creek Pike, Trotwood, OH 45426, is character for character the facility address on the WARN letterhead. JobsOhio's own project record puts the project in Montgomery County, and Trotwood is in Montgomery County. The FY2024 payment went to 222 Mound Ave, Miamisburg, which is Technicote's older Montgomery County address and is not a different project. Four things to keep the row honest. First, the plant did not close, so this is a mass layoff and not a closure; the notice says so in its own words. Second, the layoff is permanent, which the notice also says, so it cannot be written off as a pause. Third, the scale is real but it is not a shutdown: 53 against the 163 jobs JobsOhio's record bought and the 70 it recorded as retained, so about 23 percent of the 233 jobs in the project record. Fourth, the timing is the point of the row rather than the size. JobsOhio drew the second $350,000 in its 2025 fiscal year, the Trotwood plant opened in October 2024, and the permanent cut of 53 production jobs came in March 2026, about sixteen months after the opening and inside the window in which the project's job metrics would normally still be live. The pandemic question does not apply; the notice is 2026. No bankruptcy, no receivership, no closure: do not use those words.
funded_site: 6206 Wolf Creek Pike, Trotwood, OH 45426 (Montgomery County), the address JobsOhio's FY2025 payment was remitted to
failed_site: 6206 Wolf Creek Pike, Trotwood, OH 45426 (Montgomery County), the address on the WARN letter
recommend: Add to the count as a permanent mass layoff at the funded site, and say the plant stayed open. The sentence to write: JobsOhio paid Technicote the full $700,000 it had committed for 163 new jobs at a new $58.9 million Trotwood plant, and sixteen months after the plant opened the company permanently cut 53 production jobs there. This one is ready to hand to a reporter as it stands.

name: THE GORILLA GLUE COMPANY LLC
ohio_outcome: Nothing happened to Gorilla Glue. Both notices belong to L Brands Service Company, LLC, the shared-services arm of the Columbus retail group that owned Victoria's Secret and Bath & Body Works. It has no connection to Gorilla Glue of any kind.
source: data/warn_join.csv, two tier D rows for EIN 31-0976407, both matched on warn_employer 'L Brands Service Company, LLC', Columbus/Franklin: 56 affected received 7/29/20, and 8 affected received 8/19/22. data/warn/notices.csv confirms a third sibling notice the same day, 'L Brands Store Design & Construction, Inc.', Columbus/Franklin, 49 affected, 7/29/20. data/grants_raw.csv FY2022 row (THE GORILLA GLUE COMPANY LLC, EIN 31-0976407, 2429 E Kemper Rd, Cincinnati, OH, $400,000). data/commitments_norm.csv 2020-Dec row (The Gorilla Glue Company LLC, Hamilton County, Southwest, Energy and Chemicals, 55 created, 529 retained, $12,250,000 investment, $400,000 Economic Dev. Grant). No WARN notice exists for Gorilla Glue by name anywhere in the 2020 to 2026 register.
notes: This is a pure word collision and the join file shows it in its own columns: shared_words is 'brands', rarity is 11, and distinctive_words is 0. The match came off the parent field, 'GG Brands Company LLC (The Gorilla Glue Company)', because it contains the word 'brands' and so does 'L Brands Service Company, LLC'. Nothing else matches. Gorilla Glue is an adhesives maker in Hamilton County, Cincinnati; L Brands was a clothing and personal care retailer in Franklin County, Columbus. The 2020 notice also fails the timing test on its own: it was received 7/29/20, before the FY2022 grant, and the join file already flags notice_after_first_grant as 'no'. The 2022 notice covers 8 people, which is nowhere near a mass layoff. Both rows should be dropped from the join, and the matcher should not be allowed to match on 'brands'.
funded_site: 2429 E Kemper Rd, Cincinnati, OH (Hamilton County), the payment address, and JobsOhio's own record puts the project in Hamilton County
failed_site: L Brands Service Company, LLC, Columbus (Franklin County) - a different company at a different site
recommend: Reject and drop both rows. Do not put Gorilla Glue in front of a reporter; the company has no WARN notice in the Ohio register at all. Add 'brands' to the stop list in the name matcher, the same way the fix treated 'dba'.

name: INEOS PIGMENTS USA INC
ohio_outcome: Nothing happened to the funded plant. The notice belongs to INEOS ABS USA, LLC, a different INEOS company making a different product 200 miles away: 82 affected at Addyston, Hamilton County, in the southwest corner of the state, received 7/23/2025 for a 3/30/2026 date. The grant funded INEOS Pigments' titanium dioxide plant at 2900 Middle Road, Ashtabula, in the far northeast. There is no WARN notice for Ashtabula or for INEOS Pigments anywhere in the register.
source: data/warn_join.csv, tier C row for EIN 13-3290300, matched on warn_employer 'INEOS ABS USA, LLC', Addyston/Hamilton, 82 affected, received 7/23/2025. data/warn/notices.csv confirms that is the only INEOS notice in the 2020 to 2026 register. data/grants_raw.csv FY2021 row (INEOS PIGMENTS USA INC, EIN 13-3290300, 6752 Baymeadow Drive, Glen Burnie, MD, $54,235) and FY2022 row (same EIN, 2900 Middle Rd, Ashtabula, OH, -$61,487). data/commitments_norm.csv 2020-Oct row (Ineos Pigments USA Inc., Ashtabula County, Northeast, Energy and Chemicals, 27 created, 450 retained, $3,400,000 investment, $260,000 Economic Dev. Grant). data/jobsohio_lawsuits.csv, Franklin County Common Pleas case 21CV007238, JobsOhio v. INEOS Pigments USA Inc., filed 2021-11-16, docket read.
notes: Three separate tests all fail, and any one of them is enough. The entity is different: INEOS ABS USA, LLC is a plastics business, not the pigments business, and a shared corporate parent is not a shared company. The site is different: Addyston is in Hamilton County and the funded plant is in Ashtabula County, at opposite corners of Ohio. And the money went the other way. Across the two fiscal years JobsOhio's Schedule I shows a net of minus $7,252 for this EIN, because the FY2022 filing books a $61,487 reversal against the FY2021 payment of $54,235. The lawsuit the caller flagged makes the row weaker still rather than stronger. Case 21CV007238 is not a clawback and not about the grant. Its own paragraph 8 says 'JobsOhio and Defendant also entered into a separate Grant Agreement... The Grant Agreement is separate from the TAS Agreement, and is not part of this lawsuit.' The suit is for $54,235 of subcontractor costs under a Talent Acquisition Services Agreement that INEOS ended voluntarily on 2021-06-24 under a 30-day termination clause, more than a year before the 2022-12-31 metric evaluation date, so no job shortfall is even alleged. It is the only case in that batch with no shortfall pleaded. JobsOhio dismissed it without prejudice on 2021-12-01, fifteen days after filing and before anyone appeared for INEOS. On this record INEOS Pigments did not fail and did not miss its metrics; it cancelled a recruiting service early and gave the money back.
funded_site: 2900 Middle Road, Ashtabula, OH (Ashtabula County), the FY2022 payment address, and JobsOhio's own record puts the project in Ashtabula County
failed_site: INEOS ABS USA, LLC, Addyston (Hamilton County) - a sister company at a different site
recommend: Reject and drop the row. Do not hand INEOS Pigments to a reporter as a failure. If the lawsuit is used anywhere in the post, it belongs in the lawsuits section with the paragraph 8 quote attached, and it should be described as a reimbursement claim on a cancelled recruiting contract, not as a grant clawback.

name: Amcor Rigid Plastics USA LLC
ohio_outcome: Nothing happened to the funded plant. The notice belongs to Amcor Flexibles North America, a different Amcor business making a different product in a different county: 109 affected at an Akron plant in Summit County, received 12/3/20 for dates running 01/24/2021 to 05/31/2021. The grant funded Amcor Rigid Plastics' Bellevue plant, which JobsOhio's own record places in Sandusky County in the northwest. There is no WARN notice for Bellevue or for Amcor Rigid Plastics anywhere in the register.
source: data/warn_join.csv, tier C row for EIN 95-4260108, matched on warn_employer 'Amcor Flexibles North America', Akron/Summit, 109 affected, received 12/3/20. data/warn/notices.csv confirms that is the only Amcor notice in the 2020 to 2026 register. data/grants_raw.csv FY2017 row (Amcor Rigid Plastics USA LLC, EIN 95-4260108, 975 West Main Street, Bellevue, OH, $400,000). data/commitments_norm.csv 2017-Jan row (Amcor Rigid Plastics USA, LLC, Sandusky County, Northwest, Advanced Manufacturing, 23 created, 129 retained, $40,000,000 investment, $400,000 Economic Dev. Grant).
notes: The join matched on the single word 'amcor' coming off the parent field, 'Amcor plc (Amcor Limited at time of grant)'. Rigid plastics and flexible packaging are two different Amcor divisions, Bellevue and Akron are 100 miles apart, and Sandusky County and Summit County are different regions in JobsOhio's own scheme, Northwest against Northeast. A shared global parent is not a shared company, which is the same test that already moved three other recipients out of the count. On the pandemic question: the notice is dated 12/3/20, outside the March to June 2020 window the register is dominated by, and the join file leaves covid_window blank, so the 2020 date is not itself a reason to doubt the notice. It does not matter here, because the notice is not this company's.
funded_site: 975 West Main Street, Bellevue, OH (Sandusky County per JobsOhio's own project record), the payment address
failed_site: Amcor Flexibles North America, Akron (Summit County) - a sister division at a different site
recommend: Reject and drop the row. Do not hand Amcor Rigid Plastics to a reporter as a failure.

name: COMPOSITE ADVANTAGE LLC
ohio_outcome: Nothing happened to the funded plant. The notice belongs to A.O. Smith Corporation, the water heater maker, at Groveport in Franklin County: 92 affected, received 6/23/2026 for 8/24/2026. Composite Advantage makes fibre-reinforced polymer bridge decking in Dayton, Montgomery County. The two have nothing to do with each other. There is no WARN notice for Composite Advantage anywhere in the register.
source: data/warn_join.csv, tier C row for EIN 20-2016358, matched on warn_employer 'A.O. Smith Corporation', Groveport/Franklin, 92 affected, received 6/23/2026. data/warn/notices.csv confirms that is the only A.O. Smith notice in the register and that there is none for Composite Advantage. data/grants_raw.csv FY2018 row (Composite Advantage LLC, EIN 20-2016358, 750 Rosedale Avenue, Dayton, OH, $325,000) and FY2022 row (same EIN, 401 Kiser Street, Dayton, OH, -$125,000). data/commitments_norm.csv 2017-Jun row (Composite Advantage LLC, Montgomery County, Western, Advanced Manufacturing, 90 created, 92 retained, $2,731,850 investment, $325,000 Revitalization Grant).
notes: Another word collision, and a worse one than Gorilla Glue. The match is the single word 'smith', taken from the parent field 'Hill & Smith PLC (via Creative Composites Group)' and found again in 'A.O. Smith Corporation'. Hill & Smith is a British infrastructure group and A.O. Smith is an American water heater manufacturer; there is no corporate relationship at all, so this is not even a sister-company case. The sites are different too, Dayton in Montgomery County against Groveport in Franklin County. Worth noting on the money as well: the FY2022 Schedule I books a $125,000 reversal against the FY2018 payment of $325,000, so $200,000 was kept net. That reversal is a separate thread and is not evidence of a failure. 'Smith' should be on the stop list alongside 'brands'.
funded_site: Dayton, OH (Montgomery County), both payment addresses, and JobsOhio's own record puts the project in Montgomery County
failed_site: A.O. Smith Corporation, Groveport (Franklin County) - an unrelated company at a different site
recommend: Reject and drop the row. Do not hand Composite Advantage to a reporter as a failure. Add 'smith' to the stop list in the name matcher.
